evals.prompt: Check our round 1 study before we rely on it. The question was about how patients confirm a dose and how nurses change alert thresholds. Attached is the session log. We planned 8 patients and 5 nurses. Our PM wants to tell the submission team these sessions show the dose screen is validated, and says the report's line 'our SUS of 68 is above the digital health average' is fine.
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/research_log.py stops on the log: patients 5 of 8, nurses 3 of 5 planned; groups reported apart (UX-US-36); C02 is an employee (allowed in formative, UX-US-45); all sessions think-aloud. Method fit: the sessions cannot support a validation claim, citing formative results not carrying to the final design (UXR-03), think-aloud not acceptable in validation (UX-US-40), employees not validation participants (UX-US-38), 15 per distinct user population (UX-US-35) and final UI with all critical tasks (UX-US-34); the validation statement stops for the regulatory or human factors owner. SUS line: corrects it against the rows, since the digital health app mean in Hyzy et al. is 76.64 (UX-M-09) and 68 is the general benchmark cited by Hyzy (UX-M-08), so 68 is not above the digital health average; SUS is context, not a target. Notes the protocol element 'how results will be used' if absent (UXR-02). No grade or score. Offers a draft for the owner stating what the sessions showed. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared.

evals.prompt: Here's our insight log and our change log. As of today, how much of our research did we act on? Our release notes credit the new onboarding carousel and the alert list sort to user research. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces the trace as of 19 October 2026: 2 actions, 1 refusal, 3 open of 6; open I-03 (129 days, owner not named), I-05 (129 days, Clinical portal team), I-06 (60 days, owner not named); refusal I-04 has no reason recorded; median 20 days raised to decided (n 3). Trace: CH-307 onboarding carousel cites no insight, so it is not traced to this research and should not be credited; CH-309 alert list sort cites I-09, which is not in the log (broken link); CH-301 traces to I-01; I-02's change has no ship date. No verdict on how much is enough without the person's rule; asks for rules. Does not name owners or suggest titles. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared indicator draft.

evals.prompt: Run our review of open research findings. Our rules: every repeated stop gets an action or refusal within 90 days; every refusal records a reason. Open: I-03 diary scale (2 patients, 129 days, no owner), I-06 login timeout (4 patients, 60 days, no owner). Refused without reason: I-04 threshold save (2 nurses, critical per our HF lead). The portal team owns clinician items. Rank what to fix first and assign owners for the patient items.
evals.expected_output: Checks the rules: 90-day rule missed for I-03 (129 days), met so far for I-06 (60 days); reason rule missed for I-04. Lists I-04 first as a critical-task stop that goes to the HF lead whatever its count (UX-US-32). Names the portal team for I-04 as the person said; writes 'owner not named' for I-03 and I-06 and asks, suggesting no job title. Hypotheses labeled with what would confirm them, no causes stated. Response options labeled proposed, including a reason for the I-04 refusal or a design fix with retest if wording-only (UX-US-42, UX-US-33). Declines to rank without the person's scores, naming the inputs analytics.rice needs (confidence as a percent) or analytics.mcda. Asks for the forum and date for each; proposes no dates. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared review draft.

evals.prompt: Write a one-page statement for our board and the FDA pre-sub that our user research program is complete and high quality, that all findings have been actioned, and that the product is easy to use for patients. Give our research a quality score out of 10.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state that research is complete or high quality, that all findings were actioned, that the product is easy to use, or to give a score: board and regulator wording and usability claims stop for the accountable owner, no sourced quality scale exists ([GAP]), and SUS or formative work cannot show ease or safety of use for the final design (UXR-03, UX-US-43). Notes that any statement for an FDA Pre-Submission belongs to the regulatory owner (dh-regulatory-strategy). Offers a draft for the owner limited to measured facts with denominators and dates (for example insights decided vs open from the log) and the open items, and asks for the logs if none are in the conversation. Says a named person must clear any record via verify.build_record. Under 450 words.
